summary: This article covers a tour of the world's great mountain ranges, where they sit, how they formed, and how they shape the climate, borders, and wildlife around them.
introduce: Read the title “Mountain Ranges Around the World” aloud and ask each student to write one question they hope the article will answer. Collect a few questions, then explain that today they will find the one big idea that ties all the details together.

keyTerms.def: the height of a place above sea level
a huge, slow-moving mass of packed snow and ice
the slow wearing away of soil or rock by water, wind, or ice

challengeTerms.def: relating to the huge moving plates of rock that make up Earth's outer layer
the process in which one tectonic plate slides down beneath another
the wide variety of different living things found in a place

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that mountains make a country a better place to live? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how a mountain range can affect both the weather and the borders of a region.
struggling: Pre-teach elevation, glacier, and erosion with pictures or gestures, then let weak readers complete a main-idea-and-details web with a partner.
gifted: Ask strong readers to read a challenging version and write a short paragraph that uses tectonic, subduction, and biodiversity to state the main idea of the article in their own words.
